thread:
ana: Quick postmortem follow-up from the 2/14 throughput blip. want to lock down SLO changes and action owners before EOD.

vikram: Thanks. Can you paste the incident summary and which SLO slices were hit?

ana: TL;DR: short period (~6m) of request pileup on model-serving pool A during a region deployment. 95th and 99th latency spiked, throughput dropped ~30%. Error budget consumption bumped for the "text-gen-hosted" SLI (5 day window). Root causes look like a coordination of: a narrow autoscaler threshold, cold KV-cache misses, and a rollout that temporarily increased memory pressure.

maria: Noted. Impacted SLOs:
- text-gen-hosted.p95 <= 220ms (breached for 6m)
- text-gen-hosted.p99 <= 420ms (breached briefly)
- cluster-throughput.avg drop on pool-A (sustained ~6m)

jeff: we should avoid a permanent SLO loosen for now. prefer targeted mitigations + dashboarding and a controlled retest.

ana: Proposal:
1) Add an incident-oriented dashboard panel showing pool-level queue depth + autoscaler decisions and KV cache hit rate.
2) Adjust autoscaler policy to be more aggressive for short spikes (cooldown/scale-up thresholds).
3) Add a synthetic canary traffic job that warms KV caches on deploy for 10m.
4) Update SLO burn alerting to include a 10m rolling window so we get PagerDuty earlier for these short but sharp burns.

vikram: Owner suggestions: 1) dashboards -> tara, 2) autoscaler policy -> me (vikram), 3) canary job -> maria, 4) alerting tweak -> jeff. Timeline: dashboards + alerting in 48h, autoscaler + canary in 5 business days.

tara: I can start the dashboard skeleton now. Grafana panels: "pool queue depth", "scale decisions (events)", "kv-cache hit ratio by model" and a combined single-view for incident triage.

maria: canary job plan: a k8s CronJob in staging that runs a short traffic pattern and records KV hit/miss metrics to the same metric namespace. I’ll share the job spec tomorrow.

jeff: For alerting: change SLO burn alert from 1h -> 10m sliding window for P99 and add a low-noise escalation only if 3 consecutive windows exceed threshold. That should cut false positives but catch sharp burns.

vikram: Autoscaler changes: lower scale-up threshold from 85% CPU to 70% and reduce stabilization window from 5m to 60s for pool-A. I'll run it behind a feature flag and roll to 10% of hosts for testing.

ana: action items and deadlines (from thread):
- tara: dashboard skeleton + link to dashboard (48h)
- jeff: update SLO burn alerting rules and PR (48h)
- vikram: autoscaler feature-flagged change + rollout plan (5 business days)
- maria: canary CronJob spec + test run in staging (5 business days)
- ana: coordinate post-change test plan and update the postmortem doc with these actions (2 business days)

sre-bot: Reminder: please create JIRA tickets for each action and tag with incident-1945006789 and postmortem-followups.

jeff: I'll own the alert PR. quick Q: Do we want to temporarily pause the SLO burn automatic downstream billing/notifications while we iterate?

ana: No, keep billing notifications. We need visibility. But add a muted PD page to avoid noisy wake-ups during test rollouts.

tara: Dashboard note: will include a "repeating pattern" overlay showing last 30 days of similar micro-bursts. early look suggests 3 prior small spikes with same signature (deploy + cache misses).

maria: that's worrying — indicates a recurring pattern. i propose we add a deploy hook to warm caches pre-traffic, plus a small rollout delay for heavy models.

vikram: Agreed. Also adding a histogram of request latency by queue depth helped us in the past to correlate queueing with high p99. I'll add that panel.

ana: Can everyone add their JIRA ticket links back into this thread once created? i'll compile and update the postmortem doc.

jeff: created -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3245 (alerting rule PR linked in the ticket).

tara: created -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3246 (dashboard skeleton).

maria: created -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3247 (canary job + runbook).

vikram: created -> https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-3248 (autoscaler FF + rollout).

ana: Thanks all. i'll update the postmortem doc with owners, timelines, and add a "recurring pattern" section calling out deploy+cache-miss signature. we'll reconvene in 7 days for an owners check-in.

ops-bot: Reminder scheduled: 7 days from now to ping #incidents for owners check-in.

vikram: :thumbsup:

maria: :100:

jeff: thanks team.

ana: Closing note: if anyone sees another micro-burst, please drop a link to the trace and the pool-A queue snapshot. helps validate fixes.
